candidates.statement: 1.1 Purpose This document provides technical specifications for submitting data from a clinical trial to evaluate the ability to operate a motor vehicle (herein referred to as a driving study ) to support a marketing application for drug or biological product. As presented in FDA’s guidance for industry Evaluating Drug Effects on the Ability to Operate a Motor Vehicle (November 2017), 2 driving studies are primarily conducted to evaluate the effects of psychoactive drugs on the ability to operate a motor vehicle, though driving studies can also be conducted to evaluate effects of certain non-psychoactive drugs. These technical specifications should be referenced when a driving assessment is conducted as part of a clinical drug development program.
candidates.context: 1.2 Background Driving assessments are functional tests that are used to collect objective findings of a participant’s ability to operate a motor vehicle by using a measurement tool such as a computer simulator or a specially instrumented on-road vehicle. The measurement tool produces data relevant to the clinical investigation but is not under study, and example measurements collected during a driving assessment can include Standard Deviation of Lateral Position (SDLP), lane exceedance or lane drifts, response time, and number of collisions. When the drug under study has significant safety issues where the risk of assessing a participant on the road using a specially instrumented vehicle is determined to be too high, a computer simulator may be preferable.

candidates.statement: 1.3 Scope This document provides specifications for the submission of Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) and Analysis Data Model (ADaM) datasets and specifications for tables and figures. These technical specifications aim to provide general guidelines for standardized content and structure to facilitate FDA review of the marketing application that the submitted data and analysis outputs are intended to support. The SDTM and ADaM dataset specifications outlined in section 3.0 Overview of Dataset Specifications emphasize clinical outcome assessment (COA) data, including the driving assessment data and questionnaires data used to evaluate the primary and secondary endpoints defined within the driving study. The dataset specifications are not prescriptive and do not include an exhaustive list of all datasets, variables, and controlled terminologies to be submitted for FDA review. Further, the recommended tables and figures within section 4.0 Specifications for Tables and Figures do not comprise all information critical to support FDA review of a marketing application. Sponsors should discuss with FDA which specifications are applicable for their particular clinical development program.
candidates.context: Driving studies typically employ a crossover design to compare the effects of an investigational drug at one or multiple doses against both a positive control and a placebo. The timing of the planned driving assessment in each period can vary depending on the intended therapeutic use of the drug under study. 3 For instance, to evaluate the effect that an investigational sleep drug has on the ability to operate a motor vehicle, a next-day driving assessment can be conducted nine hours postdose. Alternatively, to evaluate the effects of an investigational migraine drug the driving assessment can be performed 90 minutes postdose to assess an immediate effect on the operability. It is recommended that before initiating the trial, the sponsor consult with the FDA for specific guidance on designating the primary and secondary endpoints that align with the study objectives. candidates.statement: Sponsors should provide comprehensive definitions of all endpoints within the study protocol with corresponding rationale. The measurement tool(s) used to collect driving study data and corresponding analyses should be discussed with FDA as early as possible in a clinical drug or biologic development program (e.g., the End-of-Phase 2 Meeting). Sponsors are strongly encouraged to use the resources described in section 1.4 Relationships to Other Documents and to seek Agency input for confirmation and clarification as appropriate. Sponsors should consult with the Agency to determine which requested displays defined in section 4.0 Specifications for Tables and Figures apply to the driving study data used to support their marketing application.
candidates.context: In addition, this document does not include formal definitions for driving assessment endpoints. 1.4 Relationship to Other Documents These technical specifications have been drafted in accordance with the conformance rules and assumptions outlined in the CDISC SDTM, 8 the SDTM Implementation Guide (SDTMIG), 9 the SDTMIG for Medical Devices (SDTMIG-MD), 10 the ADaM, 11 and the ADaM Implementation Guide (ADaMIG). As new versions of the models and implementation guides become available, these technical specifications can be updated to maintain alignment. In addition, the FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide (sdTCG) 12 provides general specifications and recommendations for submitting datasets using the SDTM and ADaM standards. Sponsors

candidates.statement: 3.0 OVERVIEW OF DATASET SPECIFICATIONS These dataset specifications detail the CDISC datasets that are used to support the submission of driving assessment data and questionnaires data. Sponsors should implement the CDISC SDTM standard when submitting data collected during the clinical trial and the CDISC ADaM standard when submitting analysis data. Throughout this document, the terms domain and dataset are used interchangeably and refer to the same concept. This section supplements existing guidance by providing specifications for submitting driving assessment data and questionnaires data but does not cover all data to be submitted for a clinical trial. As documented in the FDA sdTCG, 18 both SDTM and ADaM datasets should be accompanied by informative metadata provided in a compliant data definition file (i.e., Define-XML) and are expected to be accompanied by a Clinical Study Data Reviewer’s Guide (cSDRG) and an Analysis Data Reviewer’s Guide (ADRG), respectively. Standard CDISC Controlled Terminology 19 developed and maintained by CDISC and National Cancer Institute Enterprise Vocabulary Services (NCI EVS) should be used where applicable, and codelists can be extensible by adding controlled terminology that is not previously defined. Sponsor-extended codelists and use of alternative (e.g., non-CDISC or sponsor-defined) terminologies should be indicated in the study metadata (e.g., Define-XML file, cSDRG). In addition, software programs (source code) used to create the ADaM datasets and to analyze the driving study data should be submitted with the marketing application for FDA review.
candidates.context: Abbreviation Description PRO Patient-Reported Outcome QRS Questionnaires, Ratings and Scales SAP Statistical Analysis Plan SDLP Standard Deviation of Lateral Position sdTCG Study Data Technical Conformance Guide SDTM Study Data Tabulation Model SDTMIG Study Data Tabulation Model Implementation Guide SDTMIG-MD Study Data Tabulation Model Implementation Guide for Medical Devices 3.1 Driving Assessment Datasets This section specifies the datasets used to submit driving assessment data from a measurement tool such as a computer simulator or a specially instrumented on-road vehicle. These datasets include the SDTM Functional Tests (FT) dataset and the ADaM dataset containing analysis- ready driving assessment data (herein referred to as the Functional Tests Analysis Dataset (ADFT)).

candidates.context: FTENDTC End Date/Time of Test Char Date and time of end of driving assessment. Note that collecting both start and end time of a driving assessment enables the identification and subsequent analysis of partial driving assessment measurements when a driving assessment begins as planned but ends prematurely. For example, this can include environmental factors such as temperature of the room where the participant is administered the driving assessment using a simulator or the temperature in the car if an on-road vehicle is used for the driving assessment. If appropriate for analysis, the additional data should be provided in the ADFT dataset. candidates.statement: 3.1.1.3 Handling of Missing and Partial Driving Assessment Data in SDTM Understanding the reasons for and prevalence of missing and partial driving assessment data are critical to support FDA review and regulatory decision-making. FDA is especially interested in understanding the safety and/or tolerability issues that prevented a participant from completing an assessment in full, which can affect FDA’s assessment of benefit-risk. To aid in making this determination, the study protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP) should contain the definition and rationale for the criteria that compose a ” complete ” driving assessment.

candidates.statement: Pooling and grouping variables from the ADSL dataset such as AGEGRy should be copied into the ADFT dataset to support demographic subgroup analysis across the driving assessment measurements. For example, a single AGEGRy variable to categorize participants by ‘non - elderly’ vs. ‘elderly’ (e.g., where AGEGR1 is set to ‘<=65’ or ‘> 65’) can be used to assess driving assessment results when only one driving study is performed within an application. Alternatively, multiple driving studies can be conducted within an application (e.g., one study in elderly participants and one study in non-elderly participants), which can be important for certain indications such as sleep to ensure that a substantial proportion of the overall population is composed of elderly participants. The sponsor should consult with the Agency during the IND phase regarding plans for participant enrollment. Enrolling participants in driving studies from the population(s) likely to use the drug, including the elderly, is important for providing information about disease- drug interactions.

The sponsor can consult with the Agency to discuss the structure, content, and submission of this additional analysis dataset.
candidates.context: Joining adverse event (AE) data and driving assessment data can be beneficial when assessing whether an AE affects a participant ’s performance during a driving assessment. It is understood that the occurrence of an AE during a driving assessment may not result in missing or partial data. FDA is interested in knowing whether an AE occurred during the time of the driving assessment, and if so, which AE. However, joining AE data from the Analysis Data Adverse Event (ADAE) dataset to the driving assessment data in the ADFT dataset may not be feasible, given that multiple AEs can be present for a single driving assessment timepoint. Furthermore, the same AE can be ongoing and span multiple driving assessment timepoints. Thus, when applicable, submission of a standalone additional ADaM dataset that joins AE and driving assessment data and contains corresponding AE(s) for each driving assessme

candidates.statement: 3.1.2.2.1 Linking Data in SDTM via RELREC The RELREC dataset is an SDTM special-purpose dataset used to identify relationships between records in disparate SDTM datasets. If the source data (e.g., data collected using a CRF) indicate a relationship between the driving assessment data in the FT dataset and data in another SDTM dataset at the time of data collection, this association is shown using the RELREC dataset. FDA is interested in the completeness and clarity with which RELREC variables ─ including Related Domain Abbreviation (RDOMAIN), Identifying Variable (IDVAR), Identifying Variable Value (IDVARVAL), and Relationship Identifier (RELID) ─ are populated to illustrate these relationships. An example of an annotated CRF (aCRF) is shown in Figure A1. Example Annotated Case Report Form , and an example of a RELREC dataset that links driving assessment data in the SDTM FT dataset to adverse events data in the SDTM AE dataset is provided in Table A5 Subset of Sample RELREC Dataset . If the measurement tool used to capture driving assessment data directly outputs an identifier to link measurement tool events, properties, settings, or other findings to the driving assessment measurements (e.g., SDLP), the RELREC dataset should be used to illustrate the linkage of the driving assessment records in the FT dataset to the records submitted within other measurement tool dataset(s) as described in section 3.2. Datasets for Measurement Tool-Level Review .

candidates.statement: 3.1.2.4 Handling of ‘Out of Window’ Driving Assessment Data in ADaM As presented in Table 4 Specifications for a Subset of ADFT Variables , variables to assess whether a driving assessment was conducted outside of the planned window are useful for analysis. The windows used for analysis should be prespecified in the SAP, and the target time for a driving assessment to be conducted can be dependent on the indication for the drug under review. For example, the driving assessment for an investigational insomnia drug can be planned to occur 9 hours post-dose, whereas the driving assessment for an investigational migraine drug can be planned to occur 90 minutes post-dose.
candidates.context: Appendix 5.1.2 shows an example of these supporting variables within the ADFT dataset. Consider the example for an insomnia drug where a driving assessment is planned to occur 9 hours post-dose (i.e., the following morning) and the window is defined as 8 to 10 hours such that it is permissible for the participant to perform the driving assessment at any time within this window. If the driving assessment is performed either before 8 hours or after 10 hours, then the driving assessment is outside of the planned window. Note that empty values for variables such as the primary analysis timing variable used in the study (e.g., AVISIT) will aid in the determination of records that are outside of the planned window.

In the dataset, Sponsor Measurement Tool Identifier (SPDEVID) denotes the single identifier for each measurement tool and is used to link data. For example, the identifiers used to uniquely identify a driving simulator can include manufacturer, model, and serial number. Similarly, identifiers for a specially instrumented on- road vehicle can include the vehicle’s manufacturer, model name , and model year. If this is not enough information to identify the vehicle uniquely, then additional identifiers such as Vehicle Identification Number (e.g., DIPARMCD = ‘ VIN ’ ), can be included and represented by an alphanumeric string (e.g., DIVAL = ‘ABC123…789XYZ’). Sponsors should supply the minimum number of identifiers appropriate to uniquely identify each measurement tool within the DI dataset. candidates.statement: 3.5 Questionnaires Datasets This section provides dataset specifications for submitting questionnaires data (i.e., other COA data separate from the driving assessment) in CDISC format and includes other considerations for questionnaires data, such as the handling of missing data. Like driving assessments, questionnaires have documented methods for administering and scoring a test using a valid instrument and can have continuous or categorical outcomes. Within a driving study, questionnaires data can be collected to support study objectives as separate study endpoint(s), i.e., to supplement the objective driving assessment endpoint(s) (e.g., SDLP), and to measure related constructs. Questionnaires data can also be used to aid in the clinical interpretation of the objective driving assessment results and the participant’s performance . The sponsor should consider whether capturing questionnaire data before and/or immediately after a driving assessment is relevant to its clinical interpretation and to evaluate a participant’s pre-driving and post-driving outcomes. For example, before performing a driving assessment, a PRO can be used to ask questions related to readiness to drive and participant safety (e.g., ‘Do you feel safe to drive?’). Similarly, immediately after a driving assessment, a PRO can be used to ask questions related to the participant’s awareness of their recent performance (e.g., ‘How well did you drive during the driving assessment?’, ‘How motivated were you to drive to the best of your ability during the driving assessment?’).
